questions.problem: The owner of a restaurant noted that $145$ vegetarian customers visited his restaurant during a particular week. On a particular day of the same week, he noted that $x=15$ vegetarian customers visited the restaurant, corresponding to a $z$-score of $z=-1.5.$ Find the standard deviation of the number of vegetarian customers per day, giving your answer to $2$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the mean number of vegetarian customers for each day:

$$
\overset{¯}{x}=\frac{145}{7}=20.71
$$

to $2$ decimal places.

The $z$-score of an observation $x$ is defined by

$$
z=\frac{x-\overset{―}{x}}{\sigma }.
$$

The $z$-score represents how many standard deviations an observation is above or below the mean of the data set. Rewriting this in terms of $\sigma ,$ we get

$$
\sigma =\frac{x-\overset{―}{x}}{z}.
$$

So, the standard deviation $\sigma $ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\sigma  & =\frac{x-\overset{¯}{x}}{z} \\  & =\frac{15-20.71}{-1.5} \\  & =3.81\end{aligned}
$$

 
to $2$ decimal places.

questions.problem: A data set has mean $\overset{¯}{x}=16$ and standard deviation $\sigma =2.5.$ Find the value of an observation that has $z$-score $z=-0.4.$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the value of an observation $x$ which yields a given $z$-score in a data set with mean $\overset{―}{x}$ and standard deviation $\sigma ,$ we can use the following formula:

$$
x=\overset{―}{x}+z\cdot \sigma 
$$

Substituting $\overset{¯}{x}=16,$ $z=-0.4,$ and $\sigma =2.5$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\overset{―}{x}+z\cdot \sigma  \\  & =16+(-0.4)\cdot 2.5 \\  & =16-1 \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

To compute the value of an observation $x$ which yields a given $z$-score in a data set with mean $\overset{―}{x}$ and standard deviation $\sigma ,$ we can use the following formula:

$$
x=\overset{―}{x}+z\cdot \sigma 
$$

From the first observation, we have

$$
3.08=\overset{¯}{x}+(-1.2)\cdot \sigma .
$$

From the second observation, we have

$$
8.68=\overset{¯}{x}+2.3\cdot \sigma .
$$

Subtracting the first equation from the second and solving for $\sigma ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8.68-3.08 & =(2.3-(-1.2))\cdot \sigma  \\ 5.6 & =3.5\cdot \sigma  \\ \sigma  & =1.6.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this value back into our first equation and solving for $\overset{¯}{x},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3.08 & =\overset{¯}{x}+(-1.2)\cdot \sigma  \\ 3.08 & =\overset{¯}{x}+(-1.2)\cdot 1.6 \\ 3.08 & =\overset{¯}{x}-1.92 \\ \overset{¯}{x} & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
